speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Pneumonia does not typically present with severe itching and abnormal liver function tests; that diagnosis seems incorrect. Given your scleral icterus and intense pruritus, have you noticed any changes in your stool color (e.g., clay-colored) or urine color (e.g., dark tea-colored) recently?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, Ulcerative Colitis Social history: Sexually active with inconsistent condom use

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC) with concurrent Ulcerative Colitis and risk of Hepatitis C due to inconsistent condom use. The combination of severe pruritus, scleral icterus, abnormal liver function tests, and a history of autoimmune disease (Ulcerative Colitis) is highly suggestive of PBC. I recommend checking Antimitochondrial Antibodies (AMA) and a Hepatitis C panel to confirm.
